Employment

/em-PLOY-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Employment means the state of having paid work.

The new battery factory brought steady employment to a town that had lost hundreds of jobs when the mill closed.

Worked Example

Full-time employment at the hospital came with health insurance and a pension — benefits her scattered part-time gigs had never offered.

The sentence contrasts the stable state of having a paid job (with its benefits) against irregular one-off work. Employment names that state of having paid work — not the tasks themselves, but the condition of being employed.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

work: Work is the broadest word for paid labor — anything you do for money, steady or scattered. Employment is the formal state of holding a paid position: you can find work for an afternoon, but employment implies an ongoing arrangement with an employer, the condition surveys and statistics count.

occupation: An occupation is the name of your regular paid job — teacher, welder, marine biologist — the label a form asks for. Employment is the condition of having paid work at all, whatever the job is. Your occupation says what you do; your employment says that you are working.

livelihood: A livelihood is whatever keeps you fed and housed — the means of earning a living, which might mix a job, a garden, and odd repairs. Employment is one particular means: holding a paid position. A fisherman's livelihood may survive the loss of formal employment entirely.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unemployment: the state of lacking paid work

idleness: the state of not working at all

Where it sits · the stretch of working life it covers — gig → employment → career

gig vs. employment: A gig is smaller than employment — playing one wedding is a gig; it doesn't make you steadily employed.

career vs. employment: A career is broader than employment — employment is having a paid job right now; a career is the entire arc of your working life.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — em-

Prefix — em-: in, into (Latin in-, via French)

Root — ploy

Root — ploy: to fold (Latin plicare)

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Latin implicare meant "to fold in, to involve." To employ someone is literally to "fold them into" your work — and employment is the state of being folded into paid work. The same fold-root hides in pliable, complicated, and deploy ("to unfold").

Use the root in a new word: deploy

Use the root in a new word: deploy: The general waited for dawn to deploy — literally "unfold" — his troops across the ridge.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / economic

Employment can also mean the act of using something — "the employment of drones in modern farming" — but in everyday, news, and SAT contexts it almost always means having paid work, as in employment rates and full employment. Its direct opposite is unemployment.
